MAJOR: Cost evidence is not reproducible: `record()` bakes `price_usage()` output into the append-only trail, but `usage_totals()` re-runs `price_usage()` at read time, so displayed totals use the *current* catalog while stored events keep write-time costs. No pricing version/`fetched_at` snapshot is referenced per event; a catalog update silently rewrites historical totals.

`_pricing()` swallows every load exception into `{"models": {}, "aliases": {}}` with no logging, no trail marker, and no precheck signal — a missing/corrupt/renamed catalog makes all future events `cost_source=unavailable` with zero observability.
`_PRICING_CACHE` is a process-lifetime global with no invalidation; any long-lived consumer (or test run importing after a file change) sees stale prices indefinitely.
MINOR: `test_show_renders_stages_tests_and_next` was weakened: `"| 1 | gate0 | pass |"` → substring `"gate0"`, losing regression coverage of ordering, status column and padding; `test_box_table_wraps_long_cells` asserts only `count("|") > 4`, not that wrapping preserves column alignment.

Provider-cost path skips all token validation (`negative`/`cached > input` unvalidated when `provider_cost_usd` present), and `architect_review._llm_call` accepts `cost`/`total_cost`/`cost_usd` with no unit or magnitude sanity check — a per-token or currency-mismatched value is trusted as USD.
Validation (`invalid_usage`) is only reachable when the model is priced; unknown-model invalid usage reports `unavailable`, masking bad telemetry.
`store-registry.json` allow glob `"model-pricing.json"` is bare (no path) — it allowlists any file with that basename anywhere in the tree; scope it to `product-forge/config/`.
No refresh/staleness mechanism or gate for the pricing snapshot (`fetched_at: 2026-10-25`); ADR-0010 defers upstream-divergence alerts to an unspecified follow-up without a backlog item reference.
`price_usage` overwrites `u["model"]` with the normalized name only in the computed path, changing the field's semantics for downstream consumers inconsistently.

`_box` `wrap()` uses `replace_whitespace=False`, so embedded newlines/tabs in summaries/commands can break row alignment; `show()` no longer truncates summaries (the old `[:160]` cap is gone), so long summaries produce very tall tables.

The ADR cites `config/language-rule.json` `allow_new_python` as the governance exception, but the diff contains no change to that file — verify the allowlist entry actually covers the new pricing/rendering code paths (precheck confirmation only asserted in prose).
NIT: `_box` builds `top`, `sep`, `bot` as three identical strings; one constant would do.
Hard-coded widths (`[4,15,9,28,10,44]`, etc.) duplicate the 44-char cap logic and will silently mis-wrap if headers change.
`usage_totals` reads `total["cost_usd"] += ...` before the `cost_usd is None` unpriced check — works, but the ordering invites a refactor bug.
`price_usage` in `record()` means every writer pays catalog I/O on first call; a lazy-but-announced preload or explicit `refresh_pricing()` API would be cleaner for tooling reuse.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-scoped delivery: pricing catalog with provenance, provider-cost precedence, ADR-0010 governance rationale, and tests for the core formula/precedence/normalization are all present; no blocker.

Top risks: (1) write-time vs read-time pricing divergence makes historical cost evidence non-reproducible and unversioned; (2) silent catalog-load failure yields permanently unpriced trails with no observability.
Secondary concerns: weakened show/box test assertions, unvalidated provider cost units, and an over-broad registry allow glob — address before relying on the trail as audit evidence.
